Forecast production allows for potential disruptions and feasible raw material balances. © 2012 CRU International Limited **confidential** Copper Monitor March 2012 www.crugroup.com ### Marking time Having pushed above $8,000/t in January, the 3-month LME copper price traded in a narrow band $150/t either side of $8,475/t between 25th January and 8th February. On the 9th it broke out to $8,760/t but then fell to $8,175/t by 17th February, with both moves in response to the latest high and low in the Greek debt drama. A Greek rescue package was agreed and the European Central Bank (ECB) offered European banks 3-year loans that eased fears the sovereign debt crisis will morph into a banking crisis. The monetary easing in Europe saw the copper price rise back towards $8,700/t on 29th February. However, Fed Chairman Bernanke then signalled that there was not likely to be another round of monetary easing in the US, sending the US dollar up and the copper price down to below $8,500/t. The positive sentiment seems to be winning out though, as at the time of writing the price on the LME is back up towards $8,600/t. The price has been supported above $8,000/t by signs of improvement in US economic conditions, the start of a round of looser monetary conditions in China and an apparent stabilisation of the fragile European situation. This has resulted in a modest improvement in financial market sentiment, with a consequent slight increase in the net long position of non-commercial investors as seen in the chart above. The improvement in risk appetite has led to a decline in the value of the US dollar which has also supported the copper price, while LME stocks continue to decline on a daily basis. The push higher has stal

led though, due to the uncertainties about the macroeconomic outlook broadly and that of the copper market specifically.  As has been the case for the past 10 years, developments in China are the key to where the market goes from here. 

#### **China all stocked up…** 

The Chinese market is well supplied with copper following the surge in imports to record levels of over 1Mt in Q4 2011.  This flood occurred across most LME metals and suggests that it was a case of traders taking advantage of “cheap” prices to stock up following the drop across the LME complex in September and October.  The SHFE/LME arbitrage window narrowed but did not completely close in December.  As a result, January cathode imports remained strong, falling by only 18% m-o-m from the December record high, despite there being a one week holiday for the Spring Festival in the month. 



Excess cathode in China has led to a rise in both SHFE and bonded warehouse stocks.  SHFE stocks rose to 217,142t on 17<sup>th</sup> February, their highest level since August 2002.  SHFE inventory fell only marginally the following week, leaving them up by almost 160,000t from the level at the end of November last year. Bonded warehouse inventories have also more than doubled, up by 260,000t on November levels to about 460,000t now, giving a combined 420,000t increase.

With record imports in December, we were somewhat surprised that bonded warehouse stocks did not rise to current levels.  We have heard reports that customs processing was slow in December, which may account for some of the imports that came in not showing up in bonded warehouses until early January.  In addition, the SHFE/LME arbitrage window closed from the second week of January, giving traders an incentive to put imported cathode into bonded warehouses instead of trying to sell it into the physical market.  Cathode imports have been boosted by lower domestic refined production in China (down by almost 80,000t q-o-q in Q4).  Lower high-grade scrap availability has also encouraged cathode imports and consumption.  Scrap imports fell to 230,000t (gross weight) in January from 450,000t in December, as customs cracked down on smuggling and tax evasion by scrap merchants. 

#### **…and Chinese premia collapse** 

In light of the build up in stocks, the recovery in the LME price and the lack of response to the latter on SHFE, it is not surprising that we have seen a sharp slowdown of spot buying activity in China for cathode.  Spot premia for imported cathode have fallen sharply to around $30-80/t in February from the range of $110-120/t in the week before the Spring Festival in late January.  The lower end of the range would be for deals with those who are selling stock used in collateral financing deals.  These deals are continuing but we do not believe that they are accounting for much of the net increase in cathode

imports or stocks that has occurred over the past few months. Copper consumers are being cautious about buying as order books for the months ahead are not demonstrating strong growth, despite the post-holiday period usually being a seasonally strong period. The second reduction in bank reserve requirements this month will not significantly lift credit constraints. The annual People’s Congress starts on Friday 2nd March and will run for two weeks. We will have to await the end of the congress to see where economic policy is headed and how this may affect copper demand. Moreover, we have heard that there have been the first deals to ship metal out of China to take advantage of the arbitrage. This is a repeat of the exports recorded early last year. Also, some of the smelters that are allowed to export cathode with a concessionary export tax are gearing up to do so (see the 17th February _Copper China Fortnightly_ for more details). egative sentiment in the macroeconomic environment.  In Western Europe, demand for alloy rods, bars, and sections rose by 0.7% y-o-y to reach 825,000t in 2011.  While a recovery to pre-recessionary levels was never anticipated in Europe’s declining market, the 2011 total marks a consolidation at the 2010 market size which had undergone a 24.8% y-o-y rebound. 

There were mixed performances around the region.  Italy, the largest consuming nation and also heavily exposed to the European debt concerns, did not signal an equivalently large contraction in the alloy rod bar and section market as consumption was flat in the first half and down by 1.1% y-o-y in H2.  Meanwhile, Germany, the second largest market, exhibited improving demand that strengthened through the year, rising by 5.4% y-o-y in H1 and 12.2% y-o-y in H2 2011.  It was supported by the outperforming autos parts production and industrial equipment manufacturing sectors.  The Nordic countries were also a bright spot in the European alloy RBS market, as their market increased by 9,000t in 2011 after growth of 24% y-o-y in H1 and 12% y-o-y in H2. 

Weak spots in demand were evident in France, which dropped by 6,000t in full year 2011, after a rough second half that saw a contraction of 17% y-o-y.  There was also a decline in Spain, which suffered a 31% y-o-y or 7,000t drop in H2 2011.  Both of these nations were lumbered with underperforming construction industries.  Spanish construction continued its post-2008 recessionary contraction of around -2% y-o-y in H2 2011, while French construction was at a low level as its dramatic contraction after the 2008 global economic crisis reached a turning point in 2011.  The underlying weakness in demand was compounded by a large drop in the copper price, which began in April 2011 and led to an alloy scrap shortage as material was withheld from the market.  Price volatility also ensured that alloy RBS was produced in limited quantities and may have accelerated material substitution effects from brass to steel and plastic. 

#### **Copper tube market continues to contract, as Asia and North America feel the pinch during Q4 2011** 

World copper tube consumption declined by 6.2% y-o-y and 1.0% q-o-q to reach 577,000t in Q4 2011.  The seasonal Q4 pick-up in tube consumption in Asia barely materialised in 2011 as the region’s consumption level rose by 3.6% q-o-q, but this represented a 3.6% y-o-y contraction from Q4 2010.  We principally attribute this to weak demand from air conditioning manufacturers caused by stocking activity earlier in the year.  Tight credit in China, affecting consumers’ buying ability, and the highly appreciated yen in Japan, affecting consumers’ exports, also conspired to dampen the seasonal uptick in demand in Asia. 

Data from the **National Bureau of Statistics** shows that China’s output of air conditioning units declined by 2.5% y-o-y to reach 27.5M units in Q4 2011.  Production began to increase in Q4 as October’s figure rose

by 4% y-o-y.  However, this did not last as November and December both incurred year-on-year contractions of -1.3% and -4.1%, respectively.  We attribute these

declines to a mixture of base year effects, as a white goods subsidy was stimulating the Chinese home appliance market more effectively in late 2010 than in late 2011, just prior to its removal. It is also understood that finished stocks that were built-up while the subsidy was still in effect had not been fully drawn down before the beginning of the seasonal up-tick in air conditioning production which usually begins in November.  The combination of these factors with the Government’s continuation of the tight monetary environment means that manufacturers tended to opt to destock in Q4, limiting production and weakening copper tube demand. 

The North American copper tube market struggled in H2 2011, as regional demand fell by 13.9% and 19.4% y-o-y in Q3 and Q4 respectively.  The US comprises the largest of the North American markets for copper tube, with 86% of total consumption.  The important new homes sector has been depressed since early-2009 and, although housing starts appear to have pickedup from the beginning of January 2012, the industry was not supportive of growth in tube demand in 2011.  Air conditioner shipments, published by the US association ( **AHRI** ) indicated that unit shipments rose in each consecutive month in October to December 2011.  However, shipment levels compared to 2010 showed a 14.6% contraction in Q4 2011.  We believe that this was the key cause of the drop in copper tube consumption and production over H2, which combined with the volatile and declining copper price to deter manufacturers from restocking. 

**Mueller Industries Inc.** , the US based copper tube and fittings manufacturer, announced its end of year 2011 results, reporting net sales of US$491M in Q4 2011, down from US$527M in Q4 2010.  The company attributed US$11M of the difference in net sales between Q4 2011 and the previous year period to a decline in the copper price.  US$25M of the difference was attributed to lower unit shipment volumes, of which the plumbing and refrigeration sectors accounted for US$14M.  The company is optimistic that new housing starts will continue to rise through 2012, boosting copper tube demand. 

Despite the weak 2011 performance of the US copper tube market and the current low industry utilisation rates in North America, **Golden Dragon Precise Copper Tube Group Inc.** , the China-based copper tube fabricator, decided to go ahead with its plans to establish a copper tube mill in the US.  The company exports tube to the US from China and Mexico.  However, antidumping charges have reduced the profitabilty of such trade. ## Industry News #### **Consumption** - **Furukawa Electric** announced that it will commission a new electrolytic copper foil factory, located in Taiwan, two months ahead of schedule, in July 2012. The facility is designed to produce copper foil suitable for the manufacture of lithium ion batteries. Furukawa decided to offshore the foil production capacity last year because the appreciated yen had been limiting its competitiveness in supplying the high growth automotive lithium-ion battery market in Taiwan. The company expects to halve its electricity costs in Taiwan, which represent 30% of the total cost of electrolytic foil production in Japan. © 2012 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 13 of 16 Copper Monitor March 2012 www.crugroup.com - **SDI LaFarga LLC** expects to commence operations at its first copper wirerod plant in New Haven, Indiana, by April. The joint venture company involves the merged interests of US-based, carbon steel producer and scrap metal recycler, **Steel Dynamic’s Inc** . and Spain-based copper semis fabricator, **LaFarga Group** . The facility will mainly consume of No. 2 copper scrap from Steel Dynamic’s scrap processing facility, **OmniSource Corp.** Installed production capacity will total 180Mlbs/y, with 70% capacity utilization expected before the end of 2012. - On 16th February **, Prysmian Group** , the industry leading cable and systems provider,

won a contract worth a record-breaking €800M for the development of a high voltage DC power transmission link between Scotland and England.  The project will involve the use of at least 400km of a new Prysmiandeveloped product called Mass Impregnated PPL cable, which utilises new material technology to operate with a record longhaul wiring voltage rating of 600kV.  This means that energy losses will be kept to a minimum, resulting in a low CO2 footprint for the supply of Scotland-sourced renewable energy for England and vice-versa.  Commissioning is expected in late 2015. 

- **Nexans** , a global cablemaker and systems provider, reported sales revenue of €4,594M, up by 6.6% y- o-y in 2011.  Most of the company revenue was from sales of energy cables for the infrastructure sector (€1,956M, organic growth of 6.4% y-o-y in 2011), followed by energy cables for the industry sector (€955M, organic growth of 10.6% y-o-y in 2011), energy cable for the building sector (€941M, organic growth of 7.1% y-o-y in 2011), telecoms cable for the LAN sector (€238M, organic growth of 0.3% y-o-y in 2011) and telecoms cable for the infrastructure sector (€208M, organic growth of 11.9% y-o-y in 2011).  Given an unchanged economic environment, the group expects to install more capacity this year.  The company also recently acquired **AmerCable** , a leading manufacturer of mining, oil and gas and renewable energy cables in North America, for US$275M. 

- It was reported on 7<sup>th</sup> February that US State authorities have signed an agreement with Chinaheadquartered **Golden Dragon Precise Copper Tube Group Inc** . for the construction of a new copper tube plant in Wilcox County, Alabama.  Development of the facility will involve an investment of US$100M.  This follows September news that the company had not broken ground at its proposed US$100M, 45,000t/y copper pipe and tube project in neighbouring Clarke County, Alabama.  Larger than originally anticipated site requirements required the facility to be relocated. Production will supply the US heating, ventilation, refrigeration and air conditioning sector. 

- **TEPCO** , a Japanese power supplier announced on 17<sup>th</sup> January that it will increase its electricity prices for corporate clients by an average of 17% from 1<sup>st</sup> April to cover higher energy costs for the use of thermal power plants while the firm idles many of its nuclear power facilities.  The **Japan Copper and Brass Association** disapproves of the move, which it says would add ¥1.2 - 1.3B/y in production costs at the affected brass mills.  The 23 copper product fabrication sites within the TEPCO supply area account for 43% of total copper semis output in Japan.

- In related news, the Indonesian Energy ministry announced on 16<sup>th</sup> February that it will renegotiate the mining contract for the **Grasberg** mine with the mine’s operator, **Freeport-McMoRan** .  The move to renegotiate the 20-year-old contract is part of a broader strategy, announced last year by the new energy minister, which aims to increase the government’s share in Indonesia’s mining operations. 

- Operations were halted at the **Collahuasi** mine in Chile on the 20<sup>th</sup> -21<sup>st</sup> February following the death of a worker at the associated sulphide plant.  The mine’s management did not reveal what impact the stoppage would have on output.  Over the past year, the mine has been plagued by several disruptions due to work stoppages, bad weather and accidents.  Prior to the accident, extraction operations at the mine had already been halted due to heavy snows.  We currently expect the Collahuasi mine to produce 433,000t of copper-in-concentrate and 28,000t of EW cathode in 2012. 

- Heavy rains in the region of Calama, in Chile’s Atacama desert, halted production at a number of mines on Sunday, mainly for safety reasons. The majority had returned to normal operations by Tuesday, however, as the hazardous weather retreated.  The **Chuquicamata** mine was directly affected by the heavy rains, causing production to be halted, whereas operations at **Radomiro Tomic** were suspended as a precaution.  It is also likely that the **El Abra** mine was somewhat disrupted by the adverse weather conditions.  At **Gaby** and **Ministro Hales** some precautionary measures were put into place, but operations were not directly affected.  Nearby mines **Spence** , **El Tesoro** and **Esperanza** did not report any disruptions to production. 

- It was reported on 27<sup>th</sup> February that **Kazakhmys** had resumed operations the **Konyrat** mine in Kazakhstan where operations had stopped in 2008.  The mine is expected to remain in production for 9 years, producing around 6,000t of copper-in-concentrate in 2012 before ramping up to 9,000t/y in the subsequent years. 

- The proposed merger between **Glencore** and **Xstrata** is set to undergo scrutiny by the European Antitrust Commission. according to a statement released by the companies on 2<sup>4

th</sup> February.  This is only the first of a number of regulatory antitrust hurdles that need to be cleared before the merger can go through.  Similar processes are expected in the US and China.  The deal, described as an ‘all share merger of equals’ was announced on<sup>7th</sup> February and would see Glencore offering 2.8 new shares for each Xstrata share, equivalent to a 15.2% premium.  This would give Glencore shareholders a controlling share of 56% in the US$90B merged company called **Glencore Xstrata International,** with the remaining 44% owned by Xstrata shareholders.  Currently, Glencore owns a 34% stake in Xstrata.  The deal has yet to receive approval from Xstrata shareholders.  The new company would be a fully integrated commodity supplier with mining, processing, logistics and marketing. 

- **Minmetals Resources** ( **MMR** ) announced the acquisition of over 90% of **Anvil Mining** shares on 17<sup>th</sup> February, through its US$1.3B bid for the company.  The remaining shares will now be compulsorily acquired. MMR, which is 72% owned by China’s **Minmetals Group** ( **MMG** ), has operating copper assets in Laos and Australia and now adds Anvil’s 60,000t/y **Kinsevere** SXEW mine in DR Congo to its portfolio. 

- Commodities trader **Trafigura** announced on 24<sup>th</sup> February, that it had acquired a 90% share in **Iberian Minerals** .  The company also revealed that it intends to acquire the remaining shares in Iberian Metals that it does not currently own.  The main asset of Iberian Minerals is the **Aguas Tenidas** mine in Spain that is expected to produce 22,000t copper-in-concentrate in 2012.

#### **Exploration and Development** 

- **Mitsubishi Corp** announced on 17<sup>th</sup> February the acquisition of 18.1% of the copper project **Quellaveco** (Peru) from the **International Finance Corporation** .  The remaining 81.9% belongs to **Anglo American** , which treats Quellaveco as a high priority amongst its list of projects to develop.  It is estimated that Quellaveo requires an investment of US$3.2B and is set to produce around 225,000t/y of copper-in-concentrate. 

- **BHP Billiton** announced plans on 14<sup>th</sup> February to develop a new 152,000t/d concentrator plant at the Escondida mine in Chile to replace the **Los Colorados** concentrator.  The project, named **Organic Growth Project 1** ( **OGP1** ), will cost US$3.8B and is expected to be commissioned in H1 2015.  The company also announced the approval of the **Oxide Leach Area Project** ( **OLAP** ) which aims to maintain the mine’s leaching capacity beyond 2014, when the current heap leaching operations are due to end.  OLAP will require an investment of US$721M.  The above developments are part of BHP Billiton’s strategy aimed at increasing contained copper production capacity at Escondida to 1.3Mt by 2015-2016.

ng and Refining** 

- On 6<sup>th</sup> February, it was reported that operations had been halted at **Anglo American** ’s 140,000t/y **Chagres** smelter in Chile after subcontractors staged a labour strike.  The workers’ union of the subcontractor Tranex, a company working with transport of concentrates and ores, blocked the access to the smelter, claiming that Anglo American was restricting the right of the workers to unionize.  The strike was also indorsed by the president of Chile’s **Confederation of Copper Workers** (CTC). 

- **Pan Pacific Copper’s Saganoseki** smelter in the Oita province, Japan resumed operations on 14<sup>th</sup> February after a fire accident on 7<sup>th</sup> January. **Philippine Associated Smelting and Refining Corporation** ( **PASAR** )’s **Leyte** smelter was also affected by a fire accident that halted production. However, there has been no further information on the expected restart of the smelter.
